Multiply rational expressions, simplify, and preserve original denominator restrictions. The rule is (A/B)(C/D)=AC/(BD), for B≠0 and D≠0.

A rational expression is a quotient of polynomials. Factor numerators and denominators before multiplying. Cancel common factors, not individual terms. Canceled denominator factors still exclude values.
Factor: an expression multiplied by another. Excluded value: a zero of any original denominator. Difference of squares: a²−b²=(a−b)(a+b). Equivalent on a domain: equal for all permitted x.
Multiply numerators and multiply denominators. Factor first, cancel only identical nonzero factors, and retain all exclusions from the original denominators.
1. List zeros of every original denominator. 2. Factor all polynomials. 3. Cancel matching nonzero factors. 4. Multiply remaining factors. 5. Verify at a permitted input.
((x²−1)/(x²−4x+3))((x²−9)/(x²+4x+3))=1 after factoring and canceling. Still exclude x=−3,−1,1,3.
Do not cancel x from (x+5)/x: x+5 is a sum, not a factor. Do not forget holes after cancellation. Do not add denominators when multiplying. Inspect both original denominators.
Factor first, cancel common factors, then multiply leftovers. Record restrictions before cancellation. Algebra is faster and more reliable than graphing for this operation.
(x/3)(6/x)=2 for x≠0. ((x²−1)/(x−1))(2/(x+1))=2 for x≠−1,1. You cannot cancel x in (x+5)/x.
Original restrictions → factor completely → cancel matching factors → multiply leftovers → check. Canceled factors may disappear from the formula but not from the domain.
